# PeekedCookBook

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Formats` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public record PeekedCookBook
```

A CookBook read as MANIFESTS ALONE: every weight, rule, absent-percent and variant name in the tree, and not one decoded pixel.

## Remarks

This is [`ArchivePeek`](Nfty.Core.Formats.ArchivePeek.md)'s argument carried one level deeper. That type exists because a workspace *listing* has no business decoding a book's art, and reads the outer manifest alone. But a whole class of question is answered by the nested manifests and by nothing else — how likely a selection was, what a rule forbids, which variants a layer carries — and answering one of those through [`CookBookArchive.Read()`](Nfty.Core.Formats.CookBookArchive.md#m-read-system-string-nfty-core-parallelism) pulls every variant PNG in the collection into memory to look at a few dozen numbers.

So this is the shape those questions take their input in. It is deliberately NOT `IDisposable`: there is nothing here to own. [`LoadedCookBook`](Nfty.Core.Formats.LoadedCookBook.md) remains the engine's form — `Generator` and `Validator` take that and only that, because they draw pixels — and a reader of this one must not assume the art is even present.

**Recipe order here is ordinal, not the book's own [`CookBookManifest.RecipeOrder`](../nfty-ticket/Nfty.Core.Model.CookBookManifest.md#p-recipeorder).** That field is a listing preference and this is not a listing; anything that shows a reader a book's recipes wants [`CookBookArchive.Read()`](Nfty.Core.Formats.CookBookArchive.md#m-read-system-string-nfty-core-parallelism) or the manifest field itself.

The same book, projected off one that is already open and decoded.
